title: The Same Stars
source: The Turkish Jester, tr. George Borrow (1884)
lesson: People are more alike than different, wherever they live.
lines: Nasreddin visited a new city. The people there were very proud of it. Our towers! Our fountains! Nothing in the world compares!
He stood up in the square and announced: The air in this city is exactly like the air in my home town.
How can you possibly know that? they demanded, arms folded. A few of them were quite offended.
Simple, said Nasreddin. Last night I climbed onto a roof, and I counted the stars over this city.
And there were exactly as many as over my home town! Not one more, not one less.
The crowd tried to argue. But nobody had counted the stars themselves. So they just looked up, and said nothing.
Funny logic, true lesson. Wherever we go, we live under the same sky. People are more alike than different.
